# squinewave
A mostly bandlimited shape-shifting square-pulse-saw-sinewave oscillator with hardsync.

This oscillator generates a variable shape waveform that can morph freely between classical shapes sine, square, pulse and saw.
The shape is controlled by two interacting values: clip (squareness) and "skew" (symmetry).
All shapes use a minimum number of samples per transition (ie, the sharp end of a saw or a pulse uses minimum N samples), this makes output bandlimited.
At higher frequency, the minimum sweep rate takes over, so over a certain pitch all shapes "degrade" to sinewave. The minimum sweep rate is i-time configurable.
Hardsync (a very quick sweep to phase=0) is supported, and a sync signal is output once per cycle.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    aout [, asyncout] = squinewave(acps, aClip, aSkew, asyncin [, iMinSweep] [, iphase])
    aout [, asyncout] = squinewave(acps, aClip, aSkew [, ksyncin] [, iMinSweep] [, iphase])

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    aout [, asyncout] squinewave acps, aClip, aSkew, asyncin [, iMinSweep] [, iphase]
    aout [, asyncout] squinewave acps, aClip, aSkew [, ksyncin] [, iMinSweep] [, iphase]

```

### Initialization

_iMinSweep_ (optional) -- Range 4 and up. Sample count of the shortest square/pulse edges.  Default: sr/3000 (mostly alias-free).

_iphase_ (optional, default=-1) -- initial phase, range 0-2, proportional to the segments of the waveform (see notes). If negative value is given, skip setting phase

### Performance

_aout_ -- audio output, normalized +/-1

_asyncout_ -- (optional) - Sync signal: 1 at endpoint of each cycle, else 0.

_acps_ -- frequency. Range 0-anything; negative freq not implemented.

_aClip_ -- "squareness" of waveform shape. Range 0-1. Clip 0 is sinewave (or saw), clip 1 is squarewave (or pulse).

_aSkew_ -- symmetry of waveform shape. Range -1 to +1. Skew = 0 is symmetric like sine or square. Skew +1 or -1 is right/left-facing saw or pulse.

_asyncin_/_ksyncin_ -- (optional, ignored if not a-rate) - when >= 1, waveform quickly sweeps to phase 0. Sweep length is 0 to about 1.5*iMinSweep samples depending on current phase.

The _squinewave_ opcode is a variable shape oscillator with internally generated waveform.
The waveform has two parts:

1. cosine sweep down, followed by flat part at -1
2. cosine sweep up, followed by flat part at +1

At the end of (2), sync signal is output.

Clip (0-1) controls the proportion of flatness to sweep length in each segment.


Skew (-1 to +1) controls the proportions of segments (1) and (2) in the waveform cycle.

If skew < 0, part (1) is shorter, if skew > 0, (1) is longer than (2)

Classic waveforms have simple values:

* sine: clip=0, skew=0
* saw(like): clip=0, skew=+1 or -1 (left- or right-facing)
* square: clip=1, skew=0
* pulse: clip=1, skew=+1 or -1

Fractional values generate intermediate waveforms.

_asyncin_

Hardsync input (asyncin >= 1) makes the waveform quickly sweep to end by raising frequency to 2 * sr/iMinSweep.
Sync pulses are thus sharper than the pulse waveform.

_iMinSweep_

The waveform is bandlimited by always using a minimum number of samples for cosine sweeps, even when clip/skew are at extreme values. This is controlled by _iMinSweep_.
Since _iMinSweep_ is counted in samples, the waveform output is dependent on samplerate, but the spectrum will be very similiar independent of sr.
Default sr/3000 is fairly "soft", the actual values are 14 samples at 44.1K, 16 at 48K, 32 at 96K etc. _iMinSweep_ is counted in integers, although not strictly necessary.

If several units of _squinewave_ are run in unison, it is recommend to use different _iMinSweep_ values.
The min sweep value creates "dips" or quieter areas in the overtone series.
By using slightly different min sweep settings, spectrum is filled, rather than emphasizing the spectral profile.

### Notes

_squinewave_ is based on cosine instead of sine to generate the waveform. (This simplifies the controlling logic.)
The difference is that cosine cos(0) = 1, whereas sin(0) = 0.
This means that hardsync occurs when waveform is at peak, just about to enter its down sweep. (Sinewave hardsync would occur at a zero-crossing)

_Tip_

The length of hardsync sweeps allows chain syncing several _squinewave_ units, creating staggered hardsync pulses.

_Pitch stability_

Note that _iMinSweep_ and shape limits the ability of squinewave to match frequency exactly.
When skew or clip is active, and FM is applied, the _squinewave_ waveform will be longer or shorter than the exact period.
The differences even out however, so with symmetric FM, _squinewave_ drifts back to match average frequency.
Sinewave unshaped signal (clip=skew=0) matches poscil output to 7-8 significant digits (also under FM).

_Initial phase_

Setting initial phase is useful if squinewave is used as a shaped LFO.
Init phase is split into 4 segments with symbolic values range 0-2, so it will start at the expected place regardless of skew/clip values.
0-1 represents the first part, 1-2 the second. Some interesting _iphase_ segment values are:

* 0 - start of 1st sweep down.
* 0.5 - end of down sweep (start of "low" flat section).
* 1 - midpoint, end of 1st flat section, start 2nd, "up" sweep
* 1.5 - end of up sweep, (start of "high" flat section)
* 0.25 and 1.25 are 0-crossings at middle of down/up sweep sections.
* 0.75 and 1.75 are middle of low/high flat sections.

If _iphase_ < 0 (skip) at first use, initial phase is set to 1.25, ie 0-crossing of the "up" sweep. This makes output look like a sinewave.

## Examples

Here is an example of the _squinewave_ opcode. It uses the file [squinewave.csd](../examples/squinewave.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac      ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o sqrt.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>

;#################################################
nchnls = 2
ksmps = 100
0dbfs = 1

; aSyncin, FMod for instr 2
gafmod init 0
gasync init 0

; Modulator squinewave
instr 1
    ; freq start, end
    acps  line  p4, p3, p5
    ; shape start, end
    aclip  line  p6, p3, p7
    askew  line  p8, p3, p9

;  ar, async   squinewave   aFreq , aclip, askew [, asyncin, iMinSweep, iphase]
    aout1, gasync   squinewave  cpsoct(acps), aclip, askew, 0, 17

    outs1 aout1 / 1.1

    gaFMod = aout1
endin


; squinewave using gaFMod and gasync input from i1
instr 2
    ; freq & shape start, end
    acps  line  p4, p3, p5
    aclip  line  p6, p3, p7
    askew  line  p8, p3, p9

    aFMindex line  p10, p3, p11
    asyncin = gasync * p12
    afreq = cpsoct(acps + aFMindex * gaFMod)

;  ar  squinewave   aFreq, aclip, askew [, asyncin, iMinSweep, iphase]
    aout2  squinewave   afreq , aclip, askew, asyncin

    outs2 aout2 / 1.1
endin


</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>


; First part instr 1 hardsyncs instr 2 (p12)

;          p4=fund   clip     skew 
i1 0  1.  6.11 6.06  0   1    -1  +1
i1 +  1.  pp5  2.03  pp7  0   pp9  0
i1 +  1.  pp5  7.11  pp7  .8  pp9 -.8
i1 +  2.  pp5  8.11  pp7  .2  pp9  1
i1 +  .5  pp5  6.05  pp7  .5  pp9  -.6
i1 +  2.5 pp5  6.05  pp7  1   pp9  1

;          p4=fund   clip     skew      p10=FM    p12=sync
i2 0  .5  1.08 2.06  0   .3   -.5  +.5  0     0   1
i2 +  .5  pp5  4.03  pp7 .5   pp9  -.6  pp11  .   .
i2 +  .5  pp5  5.11  pp7 1    pp9   .5  pp11  .   .
i2 +  .5  pp5  6.01  pp7 .8   pp9  -.5  pp11  .   .
i2 +  .5  pp5  2.11  pp7 .1   pp9   .3  pp11  .   .
i2 +  .5  pp5  3.11  pp7 .8   pp9  -.8  pp11  .   .
i2 +  2.  pp5  4.00  pp7  0   pp9   0   pp11  .   .
i2 +  3.  pp5  3.00  pp7  .3  pp9   1   pp11  .   .


s  ; End section, reset clock

; Second part instr 1 outputs FM for instr 2 (p10, p11)

;          p4=fund   clip     skew 
i1 0  1.  6.11 6.06  0    1   -.3  +.3
i1 +  1.  pp5  2.03  pp7  0   pp9  0
i1 +  1.  pp5  7.11  pp7  .8  pp9  .8
i1 +  2.  pp5  8.11  pp7  0   pp9  .4
i1 +  .5  pp5  6.05  pp7 .5   pp9 -.6
i1 +  2.5 pp5  6.05  pp7 .4   pp9  .8


;          p4=fund   clip     skew      p10=FM    p12=sync
i2 0  .5  8.08 6.06  0   .3   -.5  +.5  0     3   0
i2 +  .5  pp5  6.03  pp7 .5   pp9  -.6  pp11  2   .
```

# sr
Sets the audio sampling rate.

These statements are global value [assignments](../opcodes/assign.md), made at the beginning of an orchestra, before any instrument block is defined. Their function is to set certain [reserved symbol variables](../orch/data-types.md#constants-and-reserved-symbols) that are required for performance. Once set, these reserved symbols can be used in expressions anywhere in the orchestra.

## Syntax

```csound

sr = iarg

```

### Initialization

_sr_  = (optional) -- set sampling rate to _iarg_ samples per second per channel. The default value is 44100.

In addition, any [global variable](../orch/data-types.md) can be initialized by an _init-time assignment_ anywhere before the first [instr statement](../opcodes/instr.md).  All of the above assignments are run as instrument 0 (i-pass only) at the start of real performance.

Beginning with Csound version 3.46, _sr_ may be omitted. The sample rate will be calculated from [kr](../opcodes/kr.md) and [ksmps](../opcodes/ksmps.md), but this must evaluate to an integer. If none of these global values is defined, the sample rate will default to 44100. You will usually want to use a value that your soundcard supports, like 44100 or 48000, otherwise, the audio generated by csound may be unplayable, or you will get an error if you attempt to run in real-time. You may naturally use a sample rate like 96000, for off-line rendering even if your soundcard does not support it. Csound will generate a valid file that can be played on capable systems.

## Examples


```csound

sr = 10000
ksmps = 20
gi1 = sr/2.
ga init 0
itranspose = octpch(.0l)

```

Here is another example of the sr opcode. It uses the file [sr.csd](../examples/sr.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac  ;;;realtime audio out
; -iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if real audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o sr.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>

sr = 44100
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs  = 1

instr 1 ;use sr to find maximum harmonics

ihar    = int(sr/2/p4)          ; maximum possible number of harmonics w/o aliasing
prints  "maximum number of harmonics = %d \\n", ihar
kenv    linen .5, 1, p3, .2     ; envelope
asig    buzz  kenv, p4, ihar, 1
        outs  asig, asig

endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
f1 0 4096 10 1  ;sine wave

i 1 0 3 100     ;different frequencies
i 1 + 3 1000
i 1 + 3 10000
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

Its output should include lines like this:


```
maximum number of harmonics = 240
maximum number of harmonics = 24
maximum number of harmonics = 2

```

# st2ms
Stereo to Mid-Side Conversion.

It is a pure function with no side effects.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    am,as = st2ms(aleft,aright)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    am,as st2ms aleft,aright

```

### Performance

_am_ -- mid signal output.

_as_ -- side signal output.

_aleft_ -- left channel input.

_aright_ -- right channel input.

## Examples

Here is an example of the st2ms opcode. It uses the files [st2ms.csd](../examples/st2ms.csd) and [stereoJungle.wav](../examples/stereoJungle.wav).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if RT audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o st2ms.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>

sr = 44100
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs  = 1

; by  Menno Knevel - 2021
; sample = ambient sound of waterfall + animals (monkey)

instr 1 
al, ar    diskin2    "stereoJungle.wav", 1          ; stereo sample
am, as st2ms  al,ar
fout "MSJungleEncoded.wav", -1, am *.6, as *.6      ; write MS encoded audio file to disk
outs am *.6, as *.6                                 ; & reduce volume a bit

endin

instr 2 
al, ar    diskin2    "MSJungleEncoded.wav", 1       ; get back in the MS encoded sample
am, as ms2st  al,ar, p4
outs am, as                               

endin

</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>

i1 0 6.7          ; encode signal, write to disk

i2 10 6.7 .5      ; read encoded file from disk and decode 1:1
i2 17 6.7 .7      ; decode but with more width

e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>

```

# stack
Initializes and sets the size of the global stack. Deprecated.

Plugin opcode in stackops.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    stack(iStackSize)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    stack iStackSize

```

### Initialization

_iStackSize_  - size of the stack in bytes.

### Performance

Csound implements a single global stack. Initializing the stack with the _stack_ opcode is not required - it is optional, and if not done, the first use of [push](../opcodes/push.md) or [push_f](../opcodes/push_f.md) will automatically create a stack of 32768 bytes. Otherwise, _stack_ is normally called from the orchestra header, and takes a stack size parameter in bytes (there is an upper limit of about 16 MB). Once set, the stack size is fixed and cannot be changed during performance.

The global stack works in LIFO order: after multiple [push](../opcodes/push.md) calls, [pop](../opcodes/pop.md) should be used in reverse order.

Each [push](../opcodes/push.md) or [pop](../opcodes/pop.md) operation can work on a "bundle" of multiple variables. When using [pop](../opcodes/pop.md), the number, type, and order of items must match those used by the corresponding [push](../opcodes/push.md). That is, after a 'push Sfoo, ibar', you must call something like 'Sbar, ifoo pop', and not e.g. two separate 'pop' statements.

[push](../opcodes/push.md) and [pop](../opcodes/pop.md) opcodes can take variables of any type (i-, k-, a- and strings). Variables of type 'a' and 'k' are passed at performance time only, while 'i' and 'S' are passed at init time only.

push/pop for a, k, i, and S types copy data by value. By contrast, [push_f](../opcodes/push_f.md) only pushes a "reference" to the f-signal, and then the corresponding [pop_f](../opcodes/pop_f.md) will copy directly from the original variable to its output signal. For this reason, changing the source f-signal of [push_f](../opcodes/push_f.md) before [pop_f](../opcodes/pop_f.md) is called is not recommended, and if the instrument instance owning the variable that was passed by push_f is deactivated before pop_f is called, undefined behavior may occur.

Any stack errors (trying to push when there is no more space, or pop from an empty stack, inconsistent number or type of arguments, etc.) are fatal and terminate performance.

## Examples

Here is an example of the stack opcode. It uses the file [stack.csd](../examples/stack.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer> 
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac   ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stack.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions> 
<CsInstruments> 

sr = 44100 
ksmps = 32 
0dbfs  = 1 
nchnls = 2

stack 100000 

instr 1 

a1      oscils 0.7, 220, 0 
k1      line 0, p3, 1 
        push "blah", 123.45, a1, k1 
        push rnd(k1) 

k_rnd   pop 
S01, i01, a01, k01 pop 
        printf_i "S01 = '%s', i01 = %g\n", 1, S01, i01 
ktrig   metro 5.0 
        printf "k01 = %.3f, k_rnd = %.3f\n", ktrig, k01, k_rnd 
        outs a01, a01 

endin 
</CsInstruments> 
<CsScore> 

i 1 0 5 
e 
</CsScore> 
</CsoundSynthesizer> 

```

## See also

[Stacks](../control/stacks.md)

Using this opcode is somewhat hackish, as you can read here: [http://csound.1045644.n5.nabble.com/passing-a-string-to-a-UDO-td1099284.html](http://csound.1045644.n5.nabble.com/passing-a-string-to-a-UDO-td1099284.html).

## Credits

2006

# start
Prepares an embedded Csound engine for performance.

Use `start` after configuring and compiling a `Csound` object. The containing instrument then controls its performance with `perf(engine)`.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    iresult = start(engine)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    iresult start engine

```

### Initialization

`engine` is a `Csound` object made with `engine:Csound = create()`.

`iresult` is 0 on success and nonzero on failure. Check it before calling `perf` or reading the engine's audio. The return value lets the containing instrument decide how to handle a failed start.

`start` runs at initialization. It prepares the engine's audio I/O according to its options and allocates the buffers used to pass audio between the two engines. Call it once per engine. Calling it again on an engine that has already started returns an error and does not restart performance.

The usual setup order is to create the engine, apply [setoption](setoption.md), compile its orchestra with `compilestr(engine, Scode)` or its CSD file with `compilecsd(engine, Sfile)`, then call `start(engine)`.

Set options before compilation and startup. For an embedded engine whose audio the containing instrument will play, `setoption(engine, "-n")` prevents a separate sound output file. Audio remains available to the containing instrument.

An engine can also start before a CSD is compiled. In that case, the later CSD's `CsOptions` section is ignored and its score is sent as real-time events. Compile the CSD first when you want its options and normal score preprocessing.

### Performance

`start` does not run the engine continuously in the background. Call `kstatus = perf(engine)` on each control cycle where you want it to advance. After that call, `aSignal = inch(engine, 1)` reads the first output channel. Audio channel numbers start at 1.

Use matching sample rates for audio exchange. The example also uses the same `ksmps` in both engines.

Keep the engine alive while performing it or reading its output. Arrange [delete](delete.md) to release it when the containing instrument ends. [destroy](destroy.md) releases it immediately at initialization and must not precede later performance calls on that engine.

## Examples

A composition can prepare an embedded synthesizer before it needs to play. This example starts the engine at initialization, waits half a second in the containing instrument, then calls `perf` to play a one-second tone. The wait does not consume the embedded note's duration.

It uses [start.csd](../examples/start.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-odac -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

instr PrepareThenPlay
  engine:Csound = create()

  // Configure the embedded engine before compiling or starting it.
  // -n keeps it from writing a sound file. The main engine handles output.
  iOptions = setoption(engine, "-n -d -m0")
  if iOptions != 0 then
    prints("Could not set the embedded engine's options.\n")
    exitnow(1)
  endif

  iCompile = compilestr(engine, {{
    sr = 48000
    ksmps = 32
    nchnls = 1
    0dbfs = 1

    instr Tone
      aEnvelope = linen(0.15, 0.01, p3, 0.1)
      aTone = oscili(aEnvelope, 330)
      out(aTone)
    endin
    schedule("Tone", 0, 1)
  }})
  if iCompile != 0 then
    prints("Could not compile the embedded orchestra.\n")
    exitnow(1)
  endif

  // Prepare the engine now. Its note has not been performed yet.
  iStart = start(engine)
  if iStart != 0 then
    prints("Could not start the embedded engine.\n")
    exitnow(1)
  endif

  // Wait half a second before advancing the embedded engine.
  kElapsed = timeinsts()
  if kElapsed >= 0.5 then
    kStatus = perf(engine)
    aTone = inch(engine, 1)
    out(aTone)
  endif

  // Keep the engine until this instrument ends.
  delete(engine)
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i "PrepareThenPlay" 0 1.5
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

## See also

[setoption](setoption.md), [compilestr](compilestr.md), [compilecsd](compilecsd.md), [perf](perf.md), [inch](inch.md), [delete](delete.md), [destroy](destroy.md), [Instrument definitions, instances and opcode objects](../orch/instrument-and-opcode-objects.md)

## Credits

Author Victor Lazzarini, 2025.

New in Csound 7.

# statevar
Statevar is a new digital implementation of the analogue state-variable filter.

This filter has four simultaneous outputs: high-pass, low-pass, band-pass and band-reject. This filter uses oversampling for sharper resonance (default: 3 times oversampling). It includes a resonance limiter that prevents the filter from getting unstable.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    ahp, alp, abp, abr = statevar(ain, xcf, xq [, iosamps, istor])

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    ahp, alp, abp, abr statevar ain, xcf, xq [, iosamps, istor]

```

### Initialization

_iosamps_  -- number of times of oversampling used in the filtering process. This will determine the maximum sharpness of the filter resonance (Q). More oversampling allows higher Qs, less oversampling will limit the resonance. The default is 3 times (iosamps=0).

_istor_ --initial disposition of internal data space. Since filtering incorporates a feedback loop of previous output, the initial status of the storage space used is significant. A zero value will clear the space; a non-zero value will allow previous information to remain. The default value is 0.

### Performance

_ahp_ -- high-pass output signal.

_alp_ -- low-pass output signal.

_abp_ -- band-pass signal.

_abr_ -- band-reject signal.

_asig_ -- input signal.

_xcf_ -- filter cutoff frequency (k-rate or a-rate).

_xq_ -- filter Q (k-rate or a-rate). This value is limited internally depending on the frequency and the number of times of oversampling used in the process (3-times oversampling by default).

## Examples

Here is an example of the statevar opcode. It uses the file [statevar.csd](../examples/statevar.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac      ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o statevar.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>

sr = 44100 
ksmps = 32 
0dbfs  = 1 
nchnls = 2

instr 1

kenv linseg 0,0.1,1, p3-0.2,1, 0.1, 0           ;declick envelope       
asig buzz .6*kenv, 100, 100, 1
kf   expseg 100, p3/2, 5000, p3/2, 1000         ;envelope for filter cutoff
ahp,alp,abp,abr statevar asig, kf, 4
     outs alp,ahp                               ; lowpass left, highpass right
        
endin   
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
f 1 0 16384 10 1        ;sine wave

i1 0 5 
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>

```

## See also

[Standard Filters: Resonant Low-pass filters](../sigmod/standard.md)

# sterrain
A wave-terrain synthesis opcode using curves computed with the superformula.

See [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superformula) for more information.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    aout = sterrain(kamp, kcps, kx, ky, krx, kry, krot, ktab0, ktab1, km1, km2, \
                    kn1, kn2, kn3, ka, kb, kperiod)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    aout sterrain kamp, kcps, kx, ky, krx, kry, krot, ktab0, ktab1, km1, km2, \
                  kn1, kn2, kn3, ka, kb, kperiod

```

### Performance

_ktabx, ktaby_ -- The two tables that define the terrain - they can be changed at krate.

The output is the result of drawing the superformula curve with parameters _km1, km2, kn1, kn2, kn3, ka, kb_ (see on wikipedia), scaled with _krx_ and _kry_ and centered at _kx_, _ky_ on the terrain, rotated around the center with _krot_ radians, and traversing it at frequency _kcps/kperiod_._km1,km2_ are converted to integers.

As the speed of the point can change considerably for some parameter classes when drawing curve on the terrain some different sounds can be produced compared with other standard curves e.g. it can make triangle like parts in the output wave.

The following ranges are supported and useful:

_kn1, ka, kb_ -- !=0 and continous.

_kn2, kn3_ -- continous.

_km1, km2_ -- positive integer > 0: note that the curves are not on all combinations of km1,km2 closed and have poles (closed in infinity) for example if kn1>0 and there exists an n,m in Z with 2*km1/km2 = 2m+1/n i.e curves with (3,2) (5,2) (7,2) etc and (5,4) (6,4) (7,4) (9,4) etc. have a pole which is noticeable when listening. If kn1 < 0 then the curve is reversed and the poles go towards zero in this case. If km1 and km2 are zero silence is produced (a plain circ - same effect occurs with the tuple 2,2,2,2,2,1,1).

_kperiod_ -- some km1 and km2 ratios may cause pitch shifts. With the kperiod parameter this can be fixed. If the ratio is 1 then the kperiod value should also be set to km1 to get the incoming pitch out.

## Examples

Here is an example of the sterrain opcode wich shows the impact of letting kn1 running towards zero. It uses the file [sterrain.csd](../examples/sterrain.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-odac -d
</CsOptions>

<CsInstruments>
sr     = 44100
ksmps  = 64
nchnls = 1
```

# stix
Semi-physical model of a stick sound.

It is one of the PhISEM percussion opcodes. PhISEM (Physically Informed Stochastic Event Modeling) is an algorithmic approach for simulating collisions of multiple independent sound producing objects.

## Syntax
=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    ares = stix(iamp, idettack [, inum] [, idamp] [, imaxshake])

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    ares stix iamp, idettack [, inum] [, idamp] [, imaxshake]

```

### Initialization

_iamp_ -- Amplitude of output.  Note: As these instruments are stochastic, this is only a approximation.

_idettack_ -- period of time over which all sound is stopped

_inum_ (optional) -- The number of beads, teeth, bells, timbrels, etc.  If zero, the default value is 30.

_idamp_ (optional) -- the damping factor, as part of this equation:


```
damping_amount = 0.998 + (idamp * 0.002)

```

The default _damping_amount_ is 0.998 which means that the default value of _idamp_ is 0. The maximum _damping_amount_ is 1.0 (no damping). This means the maximum value for _idamp_ is 1.0.

The recommended range for _idamp_ is usually below 75% of the maximum value.

_imaxshake_ (optional) -- amount of energy to add back into the system. The value should be in range 0 to 1.

## Examples

Here is an example of the stix opcode. It uses the file [stix.csd](../examples/stix.csd).


```csound

</CsOptions>

ksmps = 32 
0dbfs  = 1 
nchnls = 2

instr 1

idamp = p4                      ;vary damping amount
asig stix .5, 0.01, 30, idamp
     outs asig, asig

endin
```

# stmaddcondedge

Adds edges from one node to several possible targets.

A conditional edge declares the set of nodes a node may branch to. The node chooses one of them at performance time with [stmnext](stmnext.md), and [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) checks the choice against that set. It is the same as calling [stmaddedge](stmaddedge.md) once for each target.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    stmaddcondedge(ibuilder, Sfrom, Stargets[])

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    stmaddcondedge ibuilder, Sfrom, Stargets[]

```

### Initialization

_ibuilder_ -- a builder handle, returned by [stmcreate](stmcreate.md).

_Sfrom_ -- the name of the source node.

_Stargets[]_ -- a string array with the names of the target nodes, for example `["Calm", "Build"]`. The array must be one-dimensional and not empty, otherwise an initialization error is reported. All nodes must already exist, otherwise an initialization error is reported. Targets that are already connected are skipped.

Calling it after [stmcompile](stmcompile.md) has frozen the builder causes an initialization error.

## Examples

A texture moves through three nodes, Calm, Build and Burst. Each node is a UDO that writes a shared struct and asks for the next node with [stmnext](stmnext.md) when its time is up. The runner is created inside the instrument, so it lasts as long as the note. It uses the file [stm.csd](../examples/stm.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stm.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs = 1

; A state machine that shapes a texture. The graph only says which node is
; current and which moves are allowed:
;
;   Calm -> Build -> Burst -> Calm or Build
;
; What each node does is an ordinary UDO. It writes the shared state and,
; when its time is up, asks for the next node with stmnext.

struct Texture cutoff:k, rate:k

opcode CalmNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500
  tx.rate = 1
  if t >= 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Build")
  endif
endop

opcode BuildNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500 + t * 1500     ; opens up during the node
  tx.rate = 1 + t * 3
  if t >= 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Burst")
  endif
endop

opcode BurstNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 6000
  tx.rate = 12
  if t >= 1.5 then
    ; a conditional edge: Burst may go to either node
    if random:k(0, 1) < 0.5 then
      stmnext(r, "Calm")
    else
      stmnext(r, "Build")
    endif
  endif
endop

; build the graph once, in the global space
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Calm")
stmaddnode(builder, "Build")
stmaddnode(builder, "Burst")
stmaddedge(builder, "Calm", "Build")
stmaddedge(builder, "Build", "Burst")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Burst", ["Calm", "Build"])
gi_definition@global:i = stmcompile(builder)

instr 1
  r:i = stminstance(gi_definition)
  tx:Texture = init(500, 1)

  ; the runtime loop: current node -> its UDO -> stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  t:k = stmnodetime(r)
  if strcmpk(node, "Calm") == 0 then
    CalmNode(r, tx, t)
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Build") == 0 then
    BuildNode(r, tx, t)
  else
    BurstNode(r, tx, t)
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  if status == 1 then
    printks("%5.2f s: %s -> %s\n", 0, timeinsts(), stmnodename(r, from), stmnodename(r, to))
  endif

  ; the sound only reads the shared state
  pulse:k = 0.5 + 0.5 * lfo(1, tx.rate, 0)
  cutoff:k = portk(tx.cutoff, 0.1)
  env:k = linseg(0, 0.5, 1, p3 - 1, 1, 0.5, 0)
  sig:a = vco2(0.1, 110) + vco2(0.1, 165) + vco2(0.1, 220.5)
  sig = moogladder(sig, cutoff, 0.4) * pulse * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 20
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

# stmaddedge

Adds a directed edge between two nodes of a graph builder.

An edge allows the runner to move from one node to another. Edges have a direction: to move back and forth between two nodes, add one edge in each direction.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    stmaddedge(ibuilder, Sfrom, Sto)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    stmaddedge ibuilder, Sfrom, Sto

```

### Initialization

_ibuilder_ -- a builder handle, returned by [stmcreate](stmcreate.md).

_Sfrom_, _Sto_ -- the names of the source and target nodes. Both must already have been added with [stmaddnode](stmaddnode.md), otherwise an initialization error is reported.

An edge from a node to itself makes a self transition legal: the runner stays on the node, but [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) reports a transition, the node clock restarts and the enter and exit triggers fire. Adding an edge that already exists has no effect.

Calling it after [stmcompile](stmcompile.md) has frozen the builder causes an initialization error.

## Examples

A scripted run of a small graph. It prints, for each control period, the current node and the graph clock as read before [stmadvance](stmadvance.md), the request made, and what `stmadvance` returned. Each control period lasts 10 ms. It uses the file [stm-trace.csd](../examples/stm-trace.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; A scripted run of a small graph. Each control period lasts 10 ms.
; The trace shows what stmadvance returns for each kind of request,
; and how the graph clock moves.

; Idle -> Play, Play -> Play (self edge), Play -> Hold, Hold -> Play or Idle
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Play")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "Idle")    ; id 1
stmaddnode(builder, "Hold")    ; id 2
stmentry(builder, "Idle")      ; start from Idle instead of id 0
stmaddedge(builder, "Idle", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Hold")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Hold", ["Play", "Idle"])
definition:i = stmcompile(builder)
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(definition)

instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    printks("%d nodes, %d edges: %s %s %s\n", 0, stmnodecount(r), stmedgecount(r), \
            stmnodename(r, 0), stmnodename(r, 1), stmnodename(r, 2))
    printks("cyc node   id  tick  time  nodetime  request       status from to\n", 0)
  endif

  ; read the node and the clock before stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  id:k = stmcurrentid(r)
  tick:k = stmtick(r)
  time:k = stmtime(r)
  nodetime:k = stmnodetime(r)

  request:S = strcpyk("-")
  if cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Idle")              ; there is no Play -> Idle edge
    request = strcpyk("Idle")
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")              ; self edge
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 5 then
    stmnext(r, "Hold")              ; two different requests
    stmnext(r, "Idle")
    request = strcpyk("Hold+Idle")
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, stmnodeid(r, "Hold"))  ; request by id
    request = strcpyk("id of Hold")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmreset(r, 1)                  ; back to the entry node, Idle
    request = strcpyk("reset")
  endif

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("%3d %-5s %3d %5d %5.2f %9.2f  %-12s %6d %4d %2d\n", 0, \
          cycle, node, id, tick, time, nodetime, request, status, from, to)

  if cycle == 9 then
    turnoff
  endif
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 1
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

# stmadvance

Applies the pending transition request of a runner and moves its clock.

Call it once per control period, after the code for the current node has run.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    kstatus, kfrom, kto = stmadvance(irunner)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    kstatus, kfrom, kto stmadvance irunner

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_kstatus_ -- the outcome of the advance:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | No request was pending. |
| 1 | The request was legal and the runner moved to another node. |
| 2 | The current node has no edge to the requested node. Nothing changed. |
| 3 | The request was a legal self edge: the runner stays on the same node, but the move counts as a transition. |
| 4 | Two different nodes were requested in the same control period. Neither is applied. |
| 5 | The runner is paused. |
| 6 | The runner is deleted. |

_kfrom_ -- the id of the current node before the advance.

_kto_ -- the id of the requested node. It is -1 when no single node was requested (status 0 and 4) and when the runner is paused or deleted.

The pending request is cleared whatever the outcome. A transition (status 1 or 3) restarts the node clock and is recorded in the event history, where [stmonenter](stmonenter.md), [stmonexit](stmonexit.md) and [stmevent](stmevent.md) see it.

Each call also adds one control period to the runner's clock, which is why it should be called once per control period. The period is that of the instrument or UDO that calls it. The clock does not move while the runner is paused or deleted, nor in the control period of an [stmreset](stmreset.md). Read the clock before `stmadvance`: after it, the clock shows the values of the next control period.

This opcode changes the runner, so it counts as a writer: a runner accepts writers from one instrument instance at a time. See [Writers and observers](../control/stm.md#writers-and-observers).

## Examples

### A scripted run showing every advance status

Its output is:

``` text
3 nodes, 5 edges: Play Idle Hold
cyc node   id  tick  time  nodetime  request       status from to
  1 Idle    1     0  0.00      0.00  -                 0    1 -1
  2 Idle    1     1  0.01      0.01  Play              1    1  0
  3 Play    0     2  0.02      0.00  Idle              2    0  1
  4 Play    0     3  0.03      0.01  Play              3    0  0
  5 Play    0     4  0.04      0.00  Hold+Idle         4    0 -1
  6 Play    0     5  0.05      0.01  id of Hold        1    0  2
  7 Hold    2     6  0.06      0.00  -                 0    2 -1
  8 Hold    2     7  0.07      0.01  reset             0    1 -1
  9 Idle    1     0  0.00      0.00  -                 0    1 -1
```

Cycle 3 asks for a move that has no edge (status 2), cycle 4 uses the self edge on Play (status 3), and cycle 5 asks for two different nodes (status 4). The node time restarts after every accepted move, including the self transition, but not after the rejected ones. The reset in cycle 8 returns to the entry node Idle, which is id 1, and the clock reads 0 again in cycle 9.

# stmcall

Saves the state of a runner under a name.

The saved state can be restored later with [stmrecall](stmrecall.md).

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    kdone = stmcall(irunner, Sname, ktrig)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    kdone stmcall irunner, Sname, ktrig

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_Sname_ -- the name of the saved state, from 1 to 63 characters. A name works as a save slot: saving under a name that already exists in the runner replaces that state.

_ktrig_ -- the action happens when _ktrig_ becomes greater than 0, that is on the first pass where it is positive after being 0 or less. A trigger that is positive on the very first pass also counts. Holding _ktrig_ high does not repeat the action.

_kdone_ -- 1 on the pass where the state is saved, 0 otherwise.

The saved state is the current node, the previous node, the pending request and the clock (tick count, graph time and node time). The event history and the paused state are not saved. Saving also works while the runner is paused.

A runner keeps up to 100 names. When it is full, saving under a new name replaces the oldest one. On a deleted runner, `stmcall` does nothing and outputs 0.

This opcode changes the runner, so it counts as a writer: a runner accepts writers from one instrument instance at a time. See [Writers and observers](../control/stm.md#writers-and-observers).

## Examples

A runner walks a chain of sections, one per control period. Its state at Verse is saved with [stmcall](stmcall.md) and restored twice with [stmrecall](stmrecall.md), so the walk from Verse is repeated with the same node and the same clock. It uses the file [stm-checkpoint.csd](../examples/stm-checkpoint.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; stmcall saves the state of a runner under a name, stmrecall brings it
; back. The runner walks a chain of sections, one per control period.
; The state at "Verse" is saved, and recalled twice from "Outro", so the
; walk from "Verse" is repeated with the same node and the same clock.
; A name works as a save slot: each save under "verse" replaces the last.

builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Intro")
stmaddnode(builder, "Verse")
stmaddnode(builder, "Chorus")
stmaddnode(builder, "Outro")
stmaddedge(builder, "Intro", "Verse")
stmaddedge(builder, "Verse", "Chorus")
stmaddedge(builder, "Chorus", "Outro")
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(stmcompile(builder))

instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  tick:k = stmtick(r)

  ; save each time the walk is on Verse (the trigger rises on every pass)
  saved:k = stmcall(r, "verse", strcmpk(node, "Verse") == 0 ? 1 : 0)

  ; one step along the chain per control period
  if strcmpk(node, "Intro") == 0 then
    stmnext(r, "Verse")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Verse") == 0 then
    stmnext(r, "Chorus")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Chorus") == 0 then
    stmnext(r, "Outro")
  endif

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)

  ; at Outro, go back to the saved state, but only twice
  repeats:k init 0
  recall:k = 0
  if strcmpk(node, "Outro") == 0 && repeats < 2 then
    recall = 1
    repeats += 1
  endif
  restored:k = stmrecall(r, "verse", recall)

  printks("cycle %2d  tick %d  %-6s  saved %d  restored %d  -> %s\n", 0, \
          cycle, tick, node, saved, restored, stmcurrent(r))
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 0.10
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

Its output is:

``` text
cycle  1  tick 0  Intro   saved 0  restored 0  -> Verse
cycle  2  tick 1  Verse   saved 1  restored 0  -> Chorus
cycle  3  tick 2  Chorus  saved 0  restored 0  -> Outro
cycle  4  tick 3  Outro   saved 0  restored 1  -> Verse
cycle  5  tick 1  Verse   saved 1  restored 0  -> Chorus
cycle  6  tick 2  Chorus  saved 0  restored 0  -> Outro
cycle  7  tick 3  Outro   saved 0  restored 1  -> Verse
cycle  8  tick 1  Verse   saved 1  restored 0  -> Chorus
cycle  9  tick 2  Chorus  saved 0  restored 0  -> Outro
cycle 10  tick 3  Outro   saved 0  restored 0  -> Outro

```

The trigger of `stmcall` rises on every pass through Verse, so "verse" is saved again in cycles 5 and 8; each save replaces the previous one, here with the same state. Each recall restores the node and the tick count, so the walk from Verse repeats exactly.

# stmcompile

Freezes a graph builder into an immutable definition.

The definition holds the nodes, the edges and the entry node. Runners are created from it with [stminstance](stminstance.md); one definition can back any number of runners.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    idef = stmcompile(ibuilder)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    idef stmcompile ibuilder

```

### Initialization

_ibuilder_ -- a builder handle, returned by [stmcreate](stmcreate.md).

_idef_ -- the handle of the new definition.

After `stmcompile`, the builder cannot be changed or compiled again: [stmaddnode](stmaddnode.md), [stmaddedge](stmaddedge.md), [stmaddcondedge](stmaddcondedge.md), [stmentry](stmentry.md) and a second `stmcompile` cause an initialization error. A builder without nodes cannot be compiled.

# stmcreate

Creates an empty graph builder.

The builder is the mutable stage of a state machine graph. Add nodes and edges to it, then freeze it with [stmcompile](stmcompile.md). See [State Machine Graphs](../control/stm.md) for the whole workflow.

# stmcurrent

Returns the name of the current node of a runner.

Use it to choose which code to run in the current control period, typically with [strcmpk](strcmpk.md).

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

_Snode_ -- the name of the current node, updated in every control period. It is empty at initialization.

# stmcurrentid

Returns the id of the current node of a runner.

Node ids are integers from 0, assigned in the order the nodes were added. Dispatching on the id avoids comparing strings.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    kid = stmcurrentid(irunner)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    kid stmcurrentid irunner

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_kid_ -- the id of the current node.

This opcode only reads the runner. Any number of instruments can use it at the same time.

## Examples

A scripted run of a small graph. It prints, for each control period, the current node and the graph clock as read before [stmadvance](stmadvance.md), the request made, and what `stmadvance` returned. Each control period lasts 10 ms. It uses the file [stm-trace.csd](../examples/stm-trace.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; A scripted run of a small graph. Each control period lasts 10 ms.
; The trace shows what stmadvance returns for each kind of request,
; and how the graph clock moves.

; Idle -> Play, Play -> Play (self edge), Play -> Hold, Hold -> Play or Idle
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Play")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "Idle")    ; id 1
stmaddnode(builder, "Hold")    ; id 2
stmentry(builder, "Idle")      ; start from Idle instead of id 0
stmaddedge(builder, "Idle", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Hold")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Hold", ["Play", "Idle"])
definition:i = stmcompile(builder)
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(definition)

instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
```

# stmdelete

Stops a runner for good.

A deleted runner cannot be resumed, reset or recalled. Its handle remains valid, and observers can still read its last state.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    stmdelete(irunner, ktrig)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    stmdelete irunner, ktrig

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_ktrig_ -- the action happens when _ktrig_ becomes greater than 0, that is on the first pass where it is positive after being 0 or less. A trigger that is positive on the very first pass also counts. Holding _ktrig_ high does not repeat the action.

Deleting clears the pending request and records a delete event (kind 7). From then on, [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) returns status 6 and leaves the clock alone, and every other writer is ignored.

`stmdelete` does not free the runner. Its memory is released when the handle is removed and the last opcode using it has ended.

This opcode changes the runner, so it counts as a writer: a runner accepts writers from one instrument instance at a time. See [Writers and observers](../control/stm.md#writers-and-observers).

## Examples

One instrument drives a runner through transitions, a pause, a resume and a deletion. A second instrument watches it with [stmonenter](stmonenter.md), [stmonexit](stmonexit.md) and [stmevent](stmevent.md). It uses the file [stm-events.csd](../examples/stm-events.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; Watching a runner: stmonenter and stmonexit fire on transitions, and
; stmevent reads every runner event in order, including pause, resume
; and delete. The writer and the observers are in different instruments.

; A <-> B, plus a self edge on B
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "A")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "B")    ; id 1
stmaddedge(builder, "A", "B")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "A")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "B")
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(stmcompile(builder))

; the writer: a scripted sequence of requests and controls
instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    stmnext(r, "B")
  elseif cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; self transition
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "A")               ; ignored: the runner is paused
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, "A")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; ignored: the runner is deleted
  endif

  stmpause(r, cycle == 3 ? 1 : 0)
  stmresume(r, cycle == 5 ? 1 : 0)
  stmdelete(r, cycle == 7 ? 1 : 0)

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("cycle %d: advance status %d\n", 0, cycle, status)
endin

; an observer, scheduled after the writer in each control period
instr 2
  r:i = gi_runner
  enterB:k = stmonenter(r, "B")
  exitB:k = stmonexit(r, "B")
  if enterB == 1 || exitB == 1 then
    printks("  enter B %d, exit B %d\n", 0, enterB, exitB)
  endif

  ; drain every event published since the previous pass
  more:k = 1
  while more == 1 do
    kind:k, seq:k, lost:k, more, from:k, to:k = stmevent(r)
    if more == 1 then
      printks("  event %d: kind %d, %d -> %d, overflow %d\n", 0, seq, kind, from, to, lost)
    endif
  od
endin

i 2 0 0.09
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>
```

``` text
  enter B 1, exit B 0
  event 1: kind 1, 0 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 2: advance status 3
  enter B 1, exit B 1
  event 2: kind 2, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 3: advance status 5
  event 3: kind 5, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 4: advance status 5
cycle 5: advance status 0
  event 4: kind 6, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 6: advance status 1
  enter B 0, exit B 1

  event 6: kind 7, 0 -> 0, overflow 0
cycle 8: advance status 6
cycle 9: advance status 6

```

Event kinds: 1 transition, 2 self transition, 5 pause, 6 resume, 7 delete. The self transition in cycle 2 fires both the enter and the exit trigger of B. The request in cycle 4 is ignored because the runner is paused, and the one in cycle 8 because it is deleted. Pause, resume and delete appear as events but do not fire the enter and exit triggers.

# stmevent

Reads the event history of a runner, one event per call.

Unlike [stmonenter](stmonenter.md) and [stmonexit](stmonexit.md), which only see the latest transition, `stmevent` returns every event in order and reports when some were lost.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    kkind, kseq, koverflow, kavailable, kfrom, kto = stmevent(irunner)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    kkind, kseq, koverflow, kavailable, kfrom, kto stmevent irunner

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_kavailable_ -- 1 if an unread event was returned, 0 if there was none. When it is 0, _kkind_, _kseq_, _kfrom_ and _kto_ keep their previous values.

_kkind_ -- the kind of event:

| Kind | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Transition to another node |
| 2 | Self transition |
| 3 | Reset to the entry node |
| 4 | Recall of a saved state |
| 5 | Pause |
| 6 | Resume |
| 7 | Delete |

_kseq_ -- the sequence number of the event. The first event of a runner is 1, and each following event adds 1.

_kfrom_, _kto_ -- the ids of the node before and after the event. For pause, resume and delete they are both the current node.

_koverflow_ -- 1 if events were lost before this one, 0 otherwise.

Each opcode instance has its own read position, so several observers can read the same history independently. Reading starts with the first event after the opcode was initialized. Each call returns one event, so read in a loop to get all the events of a control period, as in the example below.

A runner keeps its last 10 events. If more than 10 happen between two reads, the oldest are lost: the next call sets _koverflow_ to 1 and continues from the oldest event still kept.

This opcode only reads the runner. Any number of instruments can use it at the same time.

## Examples

One instrument drives a runner through transitions, a pause, a resume and a deletion. A second instrument watches it with [stmonenter](stmonenter.md), [stmonexit](stmonexit.md) and [stmevent](stmevent.md). It uses the file [stm-events.csd](../examples/stm-events.csd).

# stminstance

Creates a runner from a graph definition.

The runner is the part of a state machine that changes during performance: it holds the current node, the pending request, the clock and the event history. Every runner is independent, even when several are created from the same definition.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    irunner = stminstance(idef)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    irunner stminstance idef

```

### Initialization

_idef_ -- a definition handle, returned by [stmcompile](stmcompile.md).

_irunner_ -- the handle of the new runner. It starts on the entry node, with its clock at 0 and no events.

The runner belongs to the opcode instance that created it, and its handle is removed when that instance ends. Created in an instrument, a runner lasts as long as the note; created in the global space, it lasts for the whole performance. Opcodes that were initialized with the handle keep the runner alive until they end, while an opcode initialized after the handle was removed reports an initialization error.

Handles are plain numbers, so they can be passed to other instruments, for example as p-fields or global variables.

## Examples

### A state machine that shapes a texture

A texture moves through three nodes, Calm, Build and Burst. Each node is a UDO that writes a shared struct and asks for the next node with [stmnext](stmnext.md) when its time is up. The runner is created inside the instrument, so it lasts as long as the note. It uses the file [stm.csd](../examples/stm.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stm.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs = 1

; A state machine that shapes a texture. The graph only says which node is
; current and which moves are allowed:
;
;   Calm -> Build -> Burst -> Calm or Build
;
; What each node does is an ordinary UDO. It writes the shared state and,
; when its time is up, asks for the next node with stmnext.

struct Texture cutoff:k, rate:k

opcode CalmNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500
  tx.rate = 1
  if t >= 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Build")
  endif
endop

opcode BuildNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500 + t * 1500     ; opens up during the node
  tx.rate = 1 + t * 3
  if t >= 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Burst")
  endif
endop

opcode BurstNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 6000
  tx.rate = 12
  if t >= 1.5 then
    ; a conditional edge: Burst may go to either node
    if random:k(0, 1) < 0.5 then
      stmnext(r, "Calm")
    else
      stmnext(r, "Build")
    endif
  endif
endop

; build the graph once, in the global space
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Calm")
stmaddnode(builder, "Build")
stmaddnode(builder, "Burst")
stmaddedge(builder, "Calm", "Build")
stmaddedge(builder, "Build", "Burst")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Burst", ["Calm", "Build"])
gi_definition@global:i = stmcompile(builder)

instr 1
  r:i = stminstance(gi_definition)
  tx:Texture = init(500, 1)

  ; the runtime loop: current node -> its UDO -> stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  t:k = stmnodetime(r)
  if strcmpk(node, "Calm") == 0 then
    CalmNode(r, tx, t)
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Build") == 0 then
    BuildNode(r, tx, t)
  else
    BurstNode(r, tx, t)
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  if status == 1 then
```

### Nodes bound to instruments

Each node starts an instrument when it is entered and releases it when it is left. One definition backs two runners, one per voice, each with its own current node and clock. It uses the file [stm-processes.csd](../examples/stm-processes.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stm-processes.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs = 1

; Nodes bound to instruments. When a node is entered, its instrument is
; started with a held note; when the node is left, the note is released.
; One definition backs two runners, one per voice, each with its own
; current node and its own clock.
;
;   Drone -> Pulse -> Rest -> Drone

builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Drone")
stmaddnode(builder, "Pulse")
stmaddnode(builder, "Rest")
stmaddedge(builder, "Drone", "Pulse")
stmaddedge(builder, "Pulse", "Rest")
stmaddedge(builder, "Rest", "Drone")
gi_definition@global:i = stmcompile(builder)

; the supervisor of one voice: p4 = voice (1 or 2), p5 = pitch, p6 = tempo
instr 1
  r:i = stminstance(gi_definition)
  drone:i = 10 + p4 / 10      ; 10.1 or 10.2: one note per voice
  pulse:i = 11 + p4 / 10

  ; the entry node has no enter event: start its process explicitly
  schedule(drone, 0, -1, p5)

  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  t:k = stmnodetime(r) * p6
  if strcmpk(node, "Drone") == 0 && t >= 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Pulse")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Pulse") == 0 && t >= 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Rest")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Rest") == 0 && t >= 1 then
    stmnext(r, "Drone")
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)

  ; enter and exit checks in the loop that advances the graph
  if stmonenter(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    schedulek(drone, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
  endif
  if stmonenter(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    schedulek(pulse, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif

  ; release whatever is still playing when the supervisor ends
  if lastcycle() == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif

  env:k = madsr(1, 0, 1, 1)
  sig:a = vco2(0.06, p4) + vco2(0.06, p4 * 1.003)
  sig = moogladder(sig, 1200, 0.2) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin

instr 11 ; Pulse process
  env:k = madsr(0.01, 0, 1, 0.3)
  hit:k = loopseg(4, 0, 0, 1, 0.1, 0, 0.9, 0)
  sig:a = vco2(0.12, p4 * 2, 10) * hit
  sig = moogladder(sig, 3000, 0.1) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin
</CsInstruments>
```

# stmnext

Requests a transition to another node.

The request is not applied at once. The next [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) applies it if the current node has an edge to the requested node, and reports the outcome.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    stmnext(irunner, Snode)
    stmnext(irunner, knode)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    stmnext irunner, Snode
    stmnext irunner, knode

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_Snode_ -- the name of the requested node. An unknown name causes a performance error.

_knode_ -- the id of the requested node. It must be an integer from 0 to the number of nodes minus 1, otherwise a performance error is reported.

A runner has one pending request. The first request in a control period is kept, and repeating it is harmless. Requesting a different node before `stmadvance` is a conflict: the advance applies neither request and reports status 4.

Requests made while the runner is paused or deleted are ignored.

This opcode changes the runner, so it counts as a writer: a runner accepts writers from one instrument instance at a time. See [Writers and observers](../control/stm.md#writers-and-observers).

## Examples

### A state machine that shapes a texture

A texture moves through three nodes, Calm, Build and Burst. Each node is a UDO that writes a shared struct and asks for the next node with [stmnext](stmnext.md) when its time is up. The runner is created inside the instrument, so it lasts as long as the note. It uses the file [stm.csd](../examples/stm.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stm.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs = 1

; A state machine that shapes a texture. The graph only says which node is
; current and which moves are allowed:
;
;   Calm -> Build -> Burst -> Calm or Build
;
; What each node does is an ordinary UDO. It writes the shared state and,
; when its time is up, asks for the next node with stmnext.

struct Texture cutoff:k, rate:k

opcode CalmNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500
  tx.rate = 1
  if t >= 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Build")
  endif
endop

opcode BuildNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 500 + t * 1500     ; opens up during the node
  tx.rate = 1 + t * 3
  if t >= 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Burst")
  endif
endop

opcode BurstNode(r:i, tx:Texture, t:k):void
  tx.cutoff = 6000
  tx.rate = 12
  if t >= 1.5 then
    ; a conditional edge: Burst may go to either node
    if random:k(0, 1) < 0.5 then
      stmnext(r, "Calm")
    else
      stmnext(r, "Build")
    endif
  endif
endop

; build the graph once, in the global space
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Calm")
stmaddnode(builder, "Build")
stmaddnode(builder, "Burst")
stmaddedge(builder, "Calm", "Build")
stmaddedge(builder, "Build", "Burst")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Burst", ["Calm", "Build"])
gi_definition@global:i = stmcompile(builder)

instr 1
  r:i = stminstance(gi_definition)
  tx:Texture = init(500, 1)

  ; the runtime loop: current node -> its UDO -> stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  t:k = stmnodetime(r)
  if strcmpk(node, "Calm") == 0 then
    CalmNode(r, tx, t)
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Build") == 0 then
    BuildNode(r, tx, t)
  else
    BurstNode(r, tx, t)
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  if status == 1 then
    printks("%5.2f s: %s -> %s\n", 0, timeinsts(), stmnodename(r, from), stmnodename(r, to))
  endif

  ; the sound only reads the shared state
  pulse:k = 0.5 + 0.5 * lfo(1, tx.rate, 0)
  cutoff:k = portk(tx.cutoff, 0.1)
  env:k = linseg(0, 0.5, 1, p3 - 1, 1, 0.5, 0)
  sig:a = vco2(0.1, 110) + vco2(0.1, 165) + vco2(0.1, 220.5)
  sig = moogladder(sig, cutoff, 0.4) * pulse * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 20
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

### A scripted run showing every advance status

A scripted run of a small graph. It prints, for each control period, the current node and the graph clock as read before [stmadvance](stmadvance.md), the request made, and what `stmadvance` returned. Each control period lasts 10 ms. It uses the file [stm-trace.csd](../examples/stm-trace.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; A scripted run of a small graph. Each control period lasts 10 ms.
; The trace shows what stmadvance returns for each kind of request,
; and how the graph clock moves.

; Idle -> Play, Play -> Play (self edge), Play -> Hold, Hold -> Play or Idle
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Play")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "Idle")    ; id 1
stmaddnode(builder, "Hold")    ; id 2
stmentry(builder, "Idle")      ; start from Idle instead of id 0
stmaddedge(builder, "Idle", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Hold")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Hold", ["Play", "Idle"])
definition:i = stmcompile(builder)
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(definition)

instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    printks("%d nodes, %d edges: %s %s %s\n", 0, stmnodecount(r), stmedgecount(r), \
            stmnodename(r, 0), stmnodename(r, 1), stmnodename(r, 2))
    printks("cyc node   id  tick  time  nodetime  request       status from to\n", 0)
  endif

  ; read the node and the clock before stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  id:k = stmcurrentid(r)
  tick:k = stmtick(r)
  time:k = stmtime(r)
  nodetime:k = stmnodetime(r)

  request:S = strcpyk("-")
  if cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Idle")              ; there is no Play -> Idle edge
    request = strcpyk("Idle")
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")              ; self edge
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 5 then
    stmnext(r, "Hold")              ; two different requests
    stmnext(r, "Idle")
    request = strcpyk("Hold+Idle")
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, stmnodeid(r, "Hold"))  ; request by id
    request = strcpyk("id of Hold")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmreset(r, 1)                  ; back to the entry node, Idle
    request = strcpyk("reset")
  endif

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("%3d %-5s %3d %5d %5.2f %9.2f  %-12s %6d %4d %2d\n", 0, \
          cycle, node, id, tick, time, nodetime, request, status, from, to)

  if cycle == 9 then
    turnoff
  endif
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 1
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

# stmnodetime

Returns how long the current node of a runner has been current, in seconds.

It is the natural way to give a node a duration: request the next node when the node time passes a limit.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    ktime = stmnodetime(irunner)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    ktime stmnodetime irunner

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

### Performance

_ktime_ -- the graph time since the current node became current. It reads 0 in the node's first control period.

Every transition accepted by [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) restarts it, including a self transition. A rejected or conflicting request leaves it running, since the node did not change. [stmreset](stmreset.md) sets it to 0.

The clock of a runner is moved by [stmadvance](stmadvance.md), one control period per call. It is the state machine's own time: it stops while the runner is paused or deleted, and it does not follow performance time when the instrument that advances the runner is not running. Use [timeinstk](timeinstk.md) or [times](times.md) for performance time.

Read the clock before `stmadvance`: after it, the clock already shows the values of the next control period.

This opcode only reads the runner. Any number of instruments can use it at the same time.

## Examples

### A state machine that shapes a texture

A texture moves through three nodes, Calm, Build and Burst. Each node is a UDO that writes a shared struct and asks for the next node with [stmnext](stmnext.md) when its time is up. ### A scripted run showing every advance status

A scripted run of a small graph. It prints, for each control period, the current node and the graph clock as read before [stmadvance](stmadvance.md), the request made, and what `stmadvance` returned. Each control period lasts 10 ms. It uses the file [stm-trace.csd](../examples/stm-trace.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; A scripted run of a small graph. Each control period lasts 10 ms.
; The trace shows what stmadvance returns for each kind of request,
; and how the graph clock moves.

; Idle -> Play, Play -> Play (self edge), Play -> Hold, Hold -> Play or Idle
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Play")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "Idle")    ; id 1
stmaddnode(builder, "Hold")    ; id 2
stmentry(builder, "Idle")      ; start from Idle instead of id 0
stmaddedge(builder, "Idle", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Play")
stmaddedge(builder, "Play", "Hold")
stmaddcondedge(builder, "Hold", ["Play", "Idle"])
definition:i = stmcompile(builder)
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(definition)

instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    printks("%d nodes, %d edges: %s %s %s\n", 0, stmnodecount(r), stmedgecount(r), \
            stmnodename(r, 0), stmnodename(r, 1), stmnodename(r, 2))
    printks("cyc node   id  tick  time  nodetime  request       status from to\n", 0)
  endif

  ; read the node and the clock before stmadvance
  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  id:k = stmcurrentid(r)
  tick:k = stmtick(r)
  time:k = stmtime(r)
  nodetime:k = stmnodetime(r)

  request:S = strcpyk("-")
  if cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Idle")              ; there is no Play -> Idle edge
    request = strcpyk("Idle")
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "Play")              ; self edge
    request = strcpyk("Play")
  elseif cycle == 5 then
    stmnext(r, "Hold")              ; two different requests
    stmnext(r, "Idle")
    request = strcpyk("Hold+Idle")
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, stmnodeid(r, "Hold"))  ; request by id
    request = strcpyk("id of Hold")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmreset(r, 1)                  ; back to the entry node, Idle
    request = strcpyk("reset")
  endif

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("%3d %-5s %3d %5d %5.2f %9.2f  %-12s %6d %4d %2d\n", 0, \
          cycle, node, id, tick, time, nodetime, request, status, from, to)

  if cycle == 9 then
    turnoff
  endif
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 1
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

# stmonenter

Outputs 1 when a node of a runner has just been entered.

Use it to start a process when the graph moves into a node, for example by scheduling an instrument.

## Syntax

=== "Modern"
    
```csound

    ktrig = stmonenter(irunner, Snode)

```

=== "Classic"
    
```csound

    ktrig stmonenter irunner, Snode

```

### Initialization

_irunner_ -- a runner handle, returned by [stminstance](stminstance.md).

_Snode_ -- the name of the node to watch. An unknown name causes an initialization error.

### Performance

_ktrig_ -- 1 on the first pass after a transition into _Snode_, 0 otherwise.

A transition is a move accepted by [stmadvance](stmadvance.md) (status 1 or 3), or an [stmreset](stmreset.md) or [stmrecall](stmrecall.md) that changes the current node. A self transition fires both the enter and the exit trigger of its node. Pause, resume and delete are not transitions.

The node that is current when the runner is created is not an event, so nothing fires for it. Each opcode instance only reacts to transitions that happen after it was initialized: an observer that starts while a node is already current does not see an enter for it.

The opcode compares the latest transition with the one it saw on its previous pass. If the runner made several transitions in between, only the last one is seen. Call it in every control period, ideally in the instrument that advances the graph, or use [stmevent](stmevent.md) to read every event.

This opcode only reads the runner. Any number of instruments can use it at the same time.

## Examples

### Nodes bound to instruments

Each node starts an instrument when it is entered and releases it when it is left. One definition backs two runners, one per voice, each with its own current node and clock. It uses the file [stm-processes.csd](../examples/stm-processes.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
; Select audio/midi flags here according to platform
-odac     ;;;realtime audio out
;-iadc    ;;;uncomment -iadc if realtime audio input is needed too
; For Non-realtime ouput leave only the line below:
; -o stm-processes.wav -W ;;; for file output any platform
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 32
nchnls = 2
0dbfs = 1

; Nodes bound to instruments. When a node is entered, its instrument is
; started with a held note; when the node is left, the note is released.
; One definition backs two runners, one per voice, each with its own
; current node and its own clock.
;
;   Drone -> Pulse -> Rest -> Drone

builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "Drone")
stmaddnode(builder, "Pulse")
stmaddnode(builder, "Rest")
stmaddedge(builder, "Drone", "Pulse")
stmaddedge(builder, "Pulse", "Rest")
stmaddedge(builder, "Rest", "Drone")
gi_definition@global:i = stmcompile(builder)

; the supervisor of one voice: p4 = voice (1 or 2), p5 = pitch, p6 = tempo
instr 1
  r:i = stminstance(gi_definition)
  drone:i = 10 + p4 / 10      ; 10.1 or 10.2: one note per voice
  pulse:i = 11 + p4 / 10

  ; the entry node has no enter event: start its process explicitly
  schedule(drone, 0, -1, p5)

  node:S = stmcurrent(r)
  t:k = stmnodetime(r) * p6
  if strcmpk(node, "Drone") == 0 && t >= 3 then
    stmnext(r, "Pulse")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Pulse") == 0 && t >= 2 then
    stmnext(r, "Rest")
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Rest") == 0 && t >= 1 then
    stmnext(r, "Drone")
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)

  ; enter and exit checks in the loop that advances the graph
  if stmonenter(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    schedulek(drone, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
  endif
  if stmonenter(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    schedulek(pulse, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif

  ; release whatever is still playing when the supervisor ends
  if lastcycle() == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif
endin

instr 10 ; Drone process
  env:k = madsr(1, 0, 1, 1)
  sig:a = vco2(0.06, p4) + vco2(0.06, p4 * 1.003)
  sig = moogladder(sig, 1200, 0.2) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin

instr 11 ; Pulse process
  env:k = madsr(0.01, 0, 1, 0.3)
  hit:k = loopseg(4, 0, 0, 1, 0.1, 0, 0.9, 0)
  sig:a = vco2(0.12, p4 * 2, 10) * hit
  sig = moogladder(sig, 3000, 0.1) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
; p4 = voice, p5 = pitch, p6 = tempo of the graph
i 1 0 20 1 110 1
i 1 0 20 2 165 1.5
e 22
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

### Watching transitions and events

One instrument drives a runner through transitions, a pause, a resume and a deletion. A second instrument watches it with [stmonenter](stmonenter.md), [stmonexit](stmonexit.md) and [stmevent](stmevent.md). It uses the file [stm-events.csd](../examples/stm-events.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; Watching a runner: stmonenter and stmonexit fire on transitions, and
; stmevent reads every runner event in order, including pause, resume
; and delete. The writer and the observers are in different instruments.

; A <-> B, plus a self edge on B
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "A")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "B")    ; id 1
stmaddedge(builder, "A", "B")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "A")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "B")
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(stmcompile(builder))

; the writer: a scripted sequence of requests and controls
instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    stmnext(r, "B")
  elseif cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; self transition
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "A")               ; ignored: the runner is paused
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, "A")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; ignored: the runner is deleted
  endif

  stmpause(r, cycle == 3 ? 1 : 0)
  stmresume(r, cycle == 5 ? 1 : 0)
  stmdelete(r, cycle == 7 ? 1 : 0)

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("cycle %d: advance status %d\n", 0, cycle, status)
endin

; an observer, scheduled after the writer in each control period
instr 2
  r:i = gi_runner
  enterB:k = stmonenter(r, "B")
  exitB:k = stmonexit(r, "B")
  if enterB == 1 || exitB == 1 then
    printks("  enter B %d, exit B %d\n", 0, enterB, exitB)
  endif

  ; drain every event published since the previous pass
  more:k = 1
  while more == 1 do
    kind:k, seq:k, lost:k, more, from:k, to:k = stmevent(r)
    if more == 1 then
      printks("  event %d: kind %d, %d -> %d, overflow %d\n", 0, seq, kind, from, to, lost)
    endif
  od
endin
</CsInstruments>
<CsScore>
i 1 0 0.09
i 2 0 0.09
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

Its output is:

``` text
cycle 1: advance status 1
  enter B 1, exit B 0
  event 1: kind 1, 0 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 2: advance status 3
  enter B 1, exit B 1
  event 2: kind 2, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 3: advance status 5
  event 3: kind 5, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 4: advance status 5
cycle 5: advance status 0
  event 4: kind 6, 1 -> 1, overflow 0
cycle 6: advance status 1
  enter B 0, exit B 1
  event 5: kind 1, 1 -> 0, overflow 0
cycle 7: advance status 6
  event 6: kind 7, 0 -> 0, overflow 0
cycle 8: advance status 6
cycle 9: advance status 6

```

Event kinds: 1 transition, 2 self transition, 5 pause, 6 resume, 7 delete. The self transition in cycle 2 fires both the enter and the exit trigger of B. The request in cycle 4 is ignored because the runner is paused, and the one in cycle 8 because it is deleted. Pause, resume and delete appear as events but do not fire the enter and exit triggers.

```csound
  elseif strcmpk(node, "Rest") == 0 && t >= 1 then
    stmnext(r, "Drone")
  endif
  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)

  ; enter and exit checks in the loop that advances the graph
  if stmonenter(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    schedulek(drone, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Drone") == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
  endif
  if stmonenter(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    schedulek(pulse, 0, -1, p5)
  endif
  if stmonexit(r, "Pulse") == 1 then
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif

  ; release whatever is still playing when the supervisor ends
  if lastcycle() == 1 then
    turnoff2(drone, 4, 1)
    turnoff2(pulse, 4, 1)
  endif
endin

instr 10 ; Drone process
  env:k = madsr(1, 0, 1, 1)
  sig:a = vco2(0.06, p4) + vco2(0.06, p4 * 1.003)
  sig = moogladder(sig, 1200, 0.2) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin

instr 11 ; Pulse process
  env:k = madsr(0.01, 0, 1, 0.3)
  hit:k = loopseg(4, 0, 0, 1, 0.1, 0, 0.9, 0)
  sig:a = vco2(0.12, p4 * 2, 10) * hit
  sig = moogladder(sig, 3000, 0.1) * env
  out(sig, sig)
endin
</CsInstruments>

; p4 = voice, p5 = pitch, p6 = tempo of the graph

i 1 0 20 2 165 1.5
e 22
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>


```

### Watching transitions and events

One instrument drives a runner through transitions, a pause, a resume and a deletion. A second instrument watches it with [stmonenter](stmonenter.md), [stmonexit](stmonexit.md) and [stmevent](stmevent.md). It uses the file [stm-events.csd](../examples/stm-events.csd).


```csound

<CsoundSynthesizer>
<CsOptions>
-n -d -m0
</CsOptions>
<CsInstruments>
sr = 48000
ksmps = 480
nchnls = 1
0dbfs = 1

; Watching a runner: stmonenter and stmonexit fire on transitions, and
; stmevent reads every runner event in order, including pause, resume
; and delete. The writer and the observers are in different instruments.

; A <-> B, plus a self edge on B
builder:i = stmcreate()
stmaddnode(builder, "A")    ; id 0
stmaddnode(builder, "B")    ; id 1
stmaddedge(builder, "A", "B")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "A")
stmaddedge(builder, "B", "B")
gi_runner@global:i = stminstance(stmcompile(builder))

; the writer: a scripted sequence of requests and controls
instr 1
  r:i = gi_runner
  cycle:k init 0
  cycle += 1

  if cycle == 1 then
    stmnext(r, "B")
  elseif cycle == 2 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; self transition
  elseif cycle == 4 then
    stmnext(r, "A")               ; ignored: the runner is paused
  elseif cycle == 6 then
    stmnext(r, "A")
  elseif cycle == 8 then
    stmnext(r, "B")               ; ignored: the runner is deleted
  endif

  stmpause(r, cycle == 3 ? 1 : 0)
  stmresume(r, cycle == 5 ? 1 : 0)
  stmdelete(r, cycle == 7 ? 1 : 0)

  status:k, from:k, to:k = stmadvance(r)
  printks("cycle %d: advance status %d\n", 0, cycle, status)
endin

; an observer, scheduled after the writer in each control period
instr 2
  r:i = gi_runner
  enterB:k = stmonenter(r, "B")
  exitB:k = stmonexit(r, "B")
  if enterB == 1 || exitB == 1 then
    printks("  enter B %d, exit B %d\n", 0, enterB, exitB)
  endif

  ; drain every event published since the previous pass
  more:k = 1
  while more == 1 do
    kind:k, seq:k, lost:k, more, from:k, to:k = stmevent(r)
    if more == 1 then
      printks("  event %d: kind %d, %d -> %d, overflow %d\n", 0, seq, kind, from, to, lost)
    endif
  od
endin

i 1 0 0.09
i 2 0 0.09
e
</CsScore>
</CsoundSynthesizer>
```
